claims.statement: Persona keeps one account row per entity in `persona` (key, entity_kind, unit, a `revision` bumped by every committed write, and `settled_at`) and its lines in the append-only `persona_line` table, where the account is the chain heads (rows nothing supersedes) and a change is a new row whose `supersedes` names its predecessor.

A partial unique index `uq_persona_line_supersedes` allows a line to be superseded at most once, so a forked chain is unrepresentable and two writers replacing the same line cannot both land; the loser's IntegrityError is reported as a `conflict`.

A line has one of three parts — identity, character, hypothesis — with a closed kind set per part (actor identity: name, role, relationship, attribute, instruction; collective identity: name, purpose, norm; character: trait; hypothesis: explanation) and a closed mode-per-part table (identity told/deduced, character deduced/induced, hypothesis abduced), mirrored by `persona_line` CHECK constraints so a bypassing insert cannot store what the judge refuses.

Each reasoning mode carries an evidence floor enforced at write time: `told` must cite only the message(s) it was said in with `told_by` equal to their speaker and an `instruction` must be told by its subject; `deduced` needs at least two premises (citations plus `draws_on` lines) that are all current and none `abduced`; `induced` needs at least three instances on at least two Hong Kong calendar days or one Rollup aggregate key; `abduced` needs at least one current induced trait it explains, a prediction, an observable and a window end still ahead of now.

`nora.domain.persona.plan_write` is the single judge for persona writes: it judges every op against the account's chain heads and what the writer was shown and returns either the exact rows to insert or every refusal (reason from the closed `PERSONA_REFUSALS` vocabulary, a detail, and the op index), so one refused op refuses the whole call and nothing is repaired for the writer.

`SqlPersonaStore._write` runs the judge inside the write's own transaction: it inserts-or-locks the account row, reads every line and reduces it to chain heads plus aliases, calls `plan_write` with the store's screen, rolls back entirely on refusal, and only then inserts the planned rows, bumps `revision` and stamps `settled_at` when the call is a session settling the account.

A session's write is additionally guarded by `expected_revision`: the session reads the account revision before its lines, and a write against a newer revision is a `conflict` that changes nothing and leaves the next wake to read the new account.

Citations are resolved against a `PersonaCitable` that code builds from what the prompt showed the writer, accepting only a Record message id, a `response:<send id>` episode, a `rollup:<kind>:<subject>` aggregate key or a `social:<network>:<item id>` item; anything else is `unresolved_citation`, a line id in `citations` is `line_in_citations` (premises belong in `draws_on`), and message or item numbers in a line's text are `ids_in_text`.

Evidence about a person counts only if it was said in a room that lists them (`unlisted_room`), and a social item is evidence about its author alone — refused as `social_not_author` on anyone else's account and never citable by a `told` line, since it is published words rather than a message said in a room.

Every persona line's text, formatted fact, prediction and observable passes the R-18/R-28 egress screen: `SqlPersonaStore` holds `text_offence` so no writer can skip it, and `DreamerRuntime` screens a verb's arguments before the verb runs, returning a refusal with the reason instead of dropping the call.

Conflict precedence is decided by code after the writer names the conflict: told by the subject (3) outranks told by someone else (2), then deduced (1), then induced (0), a hypothesis has no rank, the loser becomes `outranked` as a new row while both lines stay, an equal-footing conflict is refused `same_rank`, a hypothesis party is refused `conflict_hypothesis`, and rewording an `outranked` line without a named conflict keeps it outranked.

Writers act on handles, never ids: `handles_for` assigns `P1`, `P2`, … to the held lines (states `current`, `disputed`, `outranked`) in part order then oldest first, deterministically, so the reader that shows the handles and the write that resolves them agree, and one line cannot be acted on twice in one call (`line_twice`).

Two caps bound an account's held prose — 5 character lines and 3 hypothesis windows counted while the window is still open, whatever the state or verdict — and exceeding them is refused `over_cap` with the way out named; identity is deliberately uncapped.

A held trait unsupported for 60 days (`TRAIT_DECAY_MS`) is retired by code when a session settles the account (`apply_decay`); a bare `keep` with no citations is not new evidence and writes nothing, re-citing evidence the line already had does not stop the clock, and a line added in the same call that rests on a decaying trait is refused `premise_not_current`.

The state vocabulary is current, disputed, outranked, hidden, superseded, retired and refuted; only current, disputed and outranked are held (a cap slot, actionable by a writer), and `superseded` and `refuted` are legal values that no Persona writer produces — the memory index derives `superseded` from a successor row and a refutation lives in the `verdict` column.

A dispute or «forget that» is a Record item (`persona_dispute`) ruled on in its own transaction with code matching the claim: the account subject's own dispute or forget hides the matched line at once, anyone else's dispute marks it `disputed` for later weighing, an unmatched or ambiguous claim lands as the row alone without touching a line, and `forget` by anyone but the subject is refused `forget_not_subject`.

A turn-written `told` line or a new dispute is a stimulus that wakes the person's session at once: `pending_told` counts `told` lines written since `persona.settled_at`, `pending_disputes` counts disputes since then, and either counts as a full wake batch instead of waiting for the message batch.

A hypothesis's verdict is never set by the writer that wrote it: the docket is a unit's open hypotheses whose prediction window has closed, a countable observable (an exact `rollup:<kind>:<subject>`) is judged by code from one Rollup read as confirmed, expired or unknown, any other observable is judged by the model handed only the window's rows, and `record_verdict` refuses `open`, a window still open, and a line already judged.

Every row records its producer in `written_by_session`: the `persona-person` adaptor for a human account, the `persona-room`, `persona-unit` and `persona-nora` collective adaptors (one shared implementation with distinct names, populations, evidence and cursors), `tag` for the graph-surface `remember`/`persona_dispute` tools of a turn, and `persona-verdict` for the judge.

Account keys are the culture key forms: `<unit>#character:<person_id>` (one account per unit-person, not per room), a room's `primary_id`, `<unit>#unit` and `<unit>#nora`, so a person's account is written once and read by every room of the unit that lists them.

A persona session's verb runs a dry-run `plan_write` so the model reads every refusal and can fix its call, stages what passes, and `commit` re-judges it inside the store at the revision the session read with `apply_decay=True`; a session that calls neither `persona_write` nor `persona_no_change` raises `AccountNotRecordableError` so the evidence watermark holds and the same revisions are handed again.

Rendering applies the write rules from the other side: only `current` and `disputed` lines render (`disputed` marked as such, while hidden, outranked and every terminal state never do), identity renders only typed facts whose effective window covers now after the authored `identity.toml` lines that carry no mode, hypotheses render only while their window is open and always as questions, and the block is `None` when an account would say nothing.

Every occasion's persona read is one bounded, fail-soft `read_persona` call whose failure drops only that account's view and increments `nora_errors_total{stage}`, and the render is budgeted per account (2,500 characters, 4,000 for Nora's own) with the turn's person blocks sharing one 12,000-character cap and a closing `[N more characters not shown]` marker.

`[persona] enabled` alone is the shadow (sessions write, nothing reads), `[persona] render` is the switch that makes prompts read accounts instead of the Honcho and prose-culture blocks, and the same pair gates whether a persona write projects its rows into the memory index in its own transaction — so flipping `render` off is the whole rollback and shadow-era lines join the index through `nora memory rebuild`.

Persona sessions and reads are observable through closed vocabularies — `nora_persona_session_total{outcome}` for written/kept/refused/unsettled/abandoned, `nora_persona_verdict_total{verdict,judge}` keeping code's and the model's verdicts apart, and `nora_errors_total{stage}` for failed reads — and two operator commands act on the tier: `nora memory persona-history` for coverage and a restart of an incomplete pass, and `nora memory persona-retry-media --key` to queue one attempt for an account's pending cached media.

Support accounting keeps provenance honest: `support_count` and `last_supported_at` grow only on citations the line did not already carry (a Rollup aggregate supports as of now, a row or episode as of when it was said), so a Rollup rebuild over the same roots cannot inflate support or refresh a trait's age, and rewording an unchanged typed identity fact preserves its assertion time and grounding instead of counting as a second assertion.

Typed identity has one contract: `validate_fact` requires the `fact_key` to match its part's kind, checks each field's shape (birthday month/day with optional year, relationship relation plus person id or unresolved name, `[]` as explicit none for list fields, attribute name/value with optional unit and numeric age/height), and plan_write additionally keeps singleton facts single-valued and refuses older evidence replacing a newer assertion.

The rules are pinned by focused tests: `tests/unit/test_persona_rules.py` is one test per judge rule (each failing if its rule is removed), `tests/infra/test_persona_store.py` covers the real-Postgres transaction, revision compare-and-set, refusals, row CHECKs, disputes and the docket, and `tests/infra/test_persona_verdict.py` exercises both judges over a seeded Rollup build.

A turn reaches the Persona tier through two graph-surface tools and the hypothesis judge through a third path: `remember` (`remember_told`) *introduces* a grounded `told` identity fact — a `PersonaAddOp`, or a `PersonaReviseOp` when a single-valued `fact_key` already holds exactly one `told` line written by the same teller — and writes it through `persona_write` at the revision it read with `written_by_session="tag"`, `apply_decay=False`, the turn's trigger messages as its citations and only a room that lists the subject in `listed_rooms`; `persona_dispute` records a dispute; and `record_verdict` (`written_by_session="persona-verdict"`) sets a hypothesis's verdict. Only the last two bypass `persona_write`, and each copies a chain head and changes only the fields it owns — a line's `state`, or its `verdict`/`verdict_by`/`verdict_at` — so neither can introduce a claim.
